clue.text: Woolly coat to take to the cleaners

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sheep's coat of wool, or a warm jacket
second meaning: to swindle someone out of their money

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to send a woolly jacket off to the dry cleaner's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take to the cleaners' is slang for cheating someone of their money, not a trip to the dry cleaner's.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a sheep's wool or a soft jacket; the verb is an idiom for overcharging or swindling a victim.

clue.text: Girl upset breaking safety device in body of aircraft

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a fuse is an electrical safety device that melts to cut the current

indicators.note: in a down clue, something upset is turned upside down, so the name is read from the bottom up

parts.note: Gale is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is so upset she wrecks a safety device inside an aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: Gale is a girl's name, read upwards in this down clue; 'safety device' points to the electrical kind that blows when overloaded.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuselage is the main central structure of an aeroplane, holding crew and passengers, as opposed to its wings and tail.

clue.text: Eternal City, ancient, in conclusion

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: a conclusion is an ending
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A grand phrase about the Eternal City, Rome, being ancient after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eternal City' looks like Rome, but 'City' belongs to the wordplay with 'ancient': the Sumerian city of Abraham.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enduring lasts and lasts, so it is close in sense to everlasting or eternal.

clue.text: Unexpectedly incriminate best high-ranking member?

indicators.note: something happening unexpectedly comes out in a surprising order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A scandal threatens to implicate the best and most senior figure in some organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that the definition is loose: a cabinet minister is a senior member of a government, which suits the scandal picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet minister sits in the top tier of a government, so is a senior member of the ruling party.

clue.text: Sack smaller, so of no use

parts.note: to give someone the boot is to sack them
less means smaller in amount

explanation.surface: A bag that has shrunk is now too small to be any good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like a bag but is the verb meaning dismiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootless is an old word meaning unavailing or futile, from boot in its archaic sense of profit or advantage.

clue.text: Discipline in class

definitions.meaning: first meaning: control and good behaviour
second meaning: a rank in biological classification, or a category

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a teacher keeping control of a classroom; 'class' is the biologist's or sorter's category.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both orderly control of a group and a taxonomic grouping ranking above family and below class.

clue.text: Work it with 'Telegraph', somehow, to illustrate Charles Blondin, perhaps

indicators.note: done somehow means done in some unspecified way, so the letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An editor tells a writer to get a piece into the Telegraph newspaper about Blondin.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Blondin was the French acrobat who crossed Niagara Falls on a high wire in 1859.
explanation.definitionFit: Blondin is a famous example of a high-wire performer, walking along a stretched rope far above the ground.

clue.text: Animals buried in huge landslide

indicators.note: something buried in a landslide lies inside it, so the answer lies inside the run of letters

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Creatures are trapped beneath the debris of an enormous landslip.
explanation.definitionFit: Elands are large African antelopes, so they are a kind of animal.

clue.text: Boy in news, extremely lucky in resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning sort again, so the letters are put into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A lad who made the headlines got very lucky while on holiday at a resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday town, but it is read as re-sort, an instruction to shuffle the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Selwyn is a man's first name, so it can stand for a boy.

clue.text: Be circumspect, at first, over hot meal cooked in a sauce

indicators.note: cooked food has been worked on and changed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to take care when a hot meal is being cooked in sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so BE and C come before H and the shuffled meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Béchamel is the classic white sauce of milk thickened with a butter and flour roux.

clue.text: Therefore gets expert to study something from the baker

parts.note: so means therefore
a dab hand is an expert, and dab alone means one
to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: Someone therefore hires an expert to examine a loaf from the bakery.
explanation.walkthrough: DAB for expert comes from the idiom dab hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda bread is a loaf raised with bicarbonate of soda instead of yeast, sold by bakers.

clue.text: Banter after good goal

indicators.note: after says the first-named word follows the second, so the clue's order is reversed when joining

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
to rail is to jest or scoff at someone, an old sense close to banter

explanation.surface: Football fans trade jibes after a fine goal is scored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goal' looks like the football scene, but it is the definition, in the sense of the holy grail.
explanation.definitionFit: A grail is a much-sought goal, from the Holy Grail of Arthurian quests.

clue.text: Learning, new actress

parts.note: lore is accumulated knowledge or learning
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A newcomer actress is learning her lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophia Loren is the Italian film star, so the surname stands for an actress.

clue.text: Not for long, one or two or three may with dog barking

parts.words: one or two or three may with dog barking
parts.note: the surface reading: a few dogs might bark one day
the setter's reading: a saying for anything fleeting or transient

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about one, two or three dogs that may be barking.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail of the clue resists a strict parse and may be garbled in the source; the answer follows from 'Not for long' and the 4,5,4,8 enumeration.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying describes anything transient that is present one day and vanishes the next.

clue.text: See 13
New Year host in this Scottish town

indicators.note: making something new means giving it a fresh form, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: the eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scottish town hosts the Hogmanay New Year celebrations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Year' reads as one phrase, but 'New' is the signal and 'Year host' is the fodder. Rothesay is the main town on the Isle of Bute.
explanation.definitionFit: Rothesay is a resort town on the Isle of Bute in the Firth of Clyde, in western Scotland.

clue.text: Immediately cancel, over the phone

indicators.note: on the phone you only hear words, so spelling is lost and a same-sounding phrase is meant

parts.note: to write off a debt is to cancel it

explanation.surface: Someone cancels an order straight away by telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Right off is an idiom for at once or straight away, as in 'I knew right off'.

clue.text: No set pieces here in passable theatrical work

parts.note: a road that is passable is open
a play is a work for the stage

explanation.surface: A critic says a decent stage show lacks big showpiece scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set pieces' sounds theatrical, but in football they are corners and free kicks, the opposite of open play.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, open play is the flowing game between dead-ball restarts such as corners and free kicks.

clue.text: Tree is hiding the Prince, elusive character

indicators.note: something hiding a thing has it tucked away inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the willow is a tree
taken as written
taken as written
P is the abbreviation for prince

explanation.surface: A prince hides behind a tree to escape notice, the elusive fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is hiding' looks like one verb phrase, but the tree does the hiding and 'is' is a separate piece placed after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A will-o'-the-wisp is a ghostly marsh light, and by extension any person or hope that slips away when chased.

clue.text: Stop talking in jail

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an order to be quiet
second meaning: locked away or confined

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as prisoners keeping quiet, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb is a blunt order to be silent, and as an adjective it means locked in or imprisoned.

clue.text: Other ranks row about a decree

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: about means around, so the noise wraps around the next piece

parts.note: a row is a loud noise, a din
taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers argue over an official order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel to suit the soldiers, but it gives the noisy sense, DIN, which wraps around A.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to order or decree something with authority.

clue.text: One of the Channel Islands — grow old on it in a retreat

parts.note: Herm is a small island near Guernsey
taken as written
to age is to grow old

explanation.surface: Someone plans to grow old in a quiet retreat on one of the Channel Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands lie off Normandy and belong to the British Crown; Herm is one of the smallest, near Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermitage is a hermit's dwelling, so any secluded place to withdraw to.

clue.text: A line on tramp in book

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line
a bum is a tramp or vagrant

explanation.surface: A line about a vagrant appears in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so A and L go before the tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a blank book for collecting photographs, stamps or autographs.

clue.text: Article absorbing female, very pale

indicators.note: absorbing something takes it inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A magazine piece about a woman who looks very pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means grey and colourless, like ash, as a frightened face looks.

clue.text: Some extra item or feature

indicators.note: some of something is only a part of it, so the answer is a stretch of the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A product comes with an extra item or added feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a distinguishing characteristic or feature of a person or thing.

clue.text: Football team, grimly humorous before game

indicators.note: before says the first-named word is placed ahead of the next one

parts.note: black comedy is grimly humorous
pool is a cue game

explanation.surface: A football team cracks dark jokes before a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackpool is a seaside town in north-west England whose club plays in tangerine.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackpool FC is an English professional football club from the Lancashire seaside resort.

clue.text: South American republic holding alternative view

indicators.note: holding something means keeping it within, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: Panama, the republic joining Central and South America
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A Latin American republic is accommodating a dissenting opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: Panama is usually counted as Central American, but it borders Colombia and was once part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide, sweeping view of a landscape.

clue.text: Wily yachtsman's beginning to get vessel ahead

parts.note: a craft is a boat or vessel

indicators.note: a word's beginning is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A cunning sailor starts out determined to get his boat in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ahead' places the vessel before the yachtsman's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Crafty means cunning and sly, a close synonym of wily.
